assertions.subject: Necrolytic acral erythema
assertions.quote: Necrolytic acral erythema can be misdiagnosed as several other dermatological conditions with similar clinical features, including erythema, scaling, and psoriasiform plaques.

assertions.subject: Necrolytic acral erythema
assertions.quote: Necrolytic acral erythema can be differentiated from psoriasis by its dark and verrucous scales and the absence of central clearing in the lesions.

assertions.subject: Erythrokeratoderma
assertions.quote: Unlike necrolytic acral erythema, erythrokeratoderma typically shows symmetrical distribution and has a genetic basis.

assertions.subject: Nummular eczema
assertions.quote: Nummular eczema is characterized by coin-shaped, erythematous, and scaly plaques, often associated with itching and discomfort.

assertions.subject: Dermatophytosis
assertions.predicate: erythematous plaques with central clearing and peripheral scaling
assertions.quote: Dermatophytosis presents with erythematous plaques with central clearing and peripheral scaling, typically caused by fungal infections.

assertions.subject: Psoriasis
assertions.predicate: well-demarcated, erythematous plaques covered with silvery scales
assertions.quote: Psoriasis often presents with well-demarcated, erythematous plaques covered with silvery scales commonly located on the elbows, knees, scalp, and lower back.

assertions.subject: Lichen simplex chronicus
assertions.quote: Lichen simplex chronicus is another skin disorder characterized by thickened, scaly patches resulting from chronic rubbing or scratching.
